title: GAME_PLAY_MANA crashes on remapped short ID, causing 10-minute loop
description:
When a mana source's short ID is remapped in ShortIdRegistry (e.g., Lotus Petal p30 gets reassigned), handleGamePlayManaAuto at BridgeCallbackHandler.java:5057 calls shortIds.resolve(entry.value()) which throws IllegalArgumentException. The uncaught exception causes the bridge to re-present the same GAME_SELECT prompt, and the LLM retries the same mana_plan, creating a loop that lasted ~10 minutes until the loop detector intervened at 26 interactions.

Evidence:
- ~/.mage-bench/logs/game_20260227_004918/Gem25P Lucky_mcp.log: 14 occurrences of "java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Unknown short ID: p30" in handleGamePlayManaAuto (lines 49-289)
- ~/.mage-bench/logs/game_20260227_004918/Gem25P Lucky_pilot.log: LLM repeatedly tried to cast Consider with mana_plan=["p30"] (lines 290-538), observing game state "reverting" after each attempt
- Loop detection eventually broke the cycle (line 307-309): "Loop detected (26 interactions on turn 5)"

Root cause: ShortIdRegistry.java:69 throws IllegalArgumentException when a short ID is not found. ShortIdRegistry.register() at lines 95-98 can evict a UUID's old short ID mapping when the server assigns a new one. If the old ID (p30) was previously mapped to Lotus Petal's UUID, but then the UUID was re-registered with a new ID (p29), the old p30 mapping is removed entirely. The LLM still references p30 from when it last saw the card.

Impact: 10-minute stall burning LLM tokens. The LLM was unable to cast Consider (a 1-mana cantrip) for the entire turn, wasting significant context and cost.

Suggested fix: Wrap shortIds.resolve() in handleGamePlayManaAuto with a try-catch for IllegalArgumentException. On failure, cancel the spell via cancelSpellFromBadManaPlan() with a clear error message back to the LLM. This prevents the loop — the LLM will see the spell was cancelled and can retry with auto-tap or updated IDs.
